Normally, as we've learned before, the normal force is usually directly opposite to the gravity force.
For example, if we have a box on a surface, there will be a gravity force here and there will be a normal force pointing exactly in the opposite direction over here.
However, on an inclined plane, things get a little different. Let's say we have an inclined plane of 35 degrees here.
And we have a box, let's draw it a bit down, over here.
Force of gravity is always pointed straight down. It's pointed towards the centre of the Earth, so it would be pointed somewhere towards here.
However, the normal force is the force that the surface exerts on the box.
So, the surface, if it's going here, the normal force should be perpendicular to the surface.
In fact, the normal force is always perpendicular to the surface because the surface is the one that's exerting the force.

then do you agree that this will be 35 degrees? It will.

Now calculate the magnitude of normal force acting on the box.

We have the normal force over here, let's call this F-N,
and we have the gravity pointing straight down over here, let's call this F-G.
So now, what we can do is we can actually translate this force, this normal force, down over here.

And the reason why we do that is since F-G is perfectly in the same direction as the vertical,
it is literally the vertical, and we know that F-N makes an angle of 35 degrees to the vertical,
we know that this is 35 degrees, and this is F-N.
And now we can calculate a lot of things, because we know that this is a right angle,
because we can make it a right angle.
And yeah, now F-N is just force of gravity, which is a hypotenuse, times cosine of 35 degrees,
because cosine is adjacent over hypotenuse.

Well, F-G is equal to mass times acceleration.

F equals M-A, cosine 35.
Well, what is our mass? We have that given, 6.0.

Cosine of 35 would be around 0.819.
And when you multiply that all together, you get around 48 newtons to sig figs, because of this.

And basically, as a rule of thumb for the future, if you have a problem with a smooth incline plane,
